title: Transaction Design for Application Workflows knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Transaction Design for Application Workflows”?
options: It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.

A transaction groups related data changes into a single reliability boundary. Isolation and locking affect what concurrent sessions can see or change; keep transactions short and design retries so the same business action is not applied twice.
questions.answer_key: A transaction groups related data changes into a single reliability boundary. Isolation and locking affect what concurrent sessions can see or change; keep transactions short and design retries so the same business action is not applied twice.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains: A transaction groups related data changes into a single reliability boundary. Isolation and locking affect what concurrent sessions can see or change; keep transactions short and design retries so the same business action is not applied twice.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “Transaction Design for Application Workflows” safely?
options: Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Describe two-session behavior for a small transaction, then test commit/rollback and one conflict in a disposable database.
Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.
questions.answer_key: Describe two-session behavior for a small transaction, then test commit/rollback and one conflict in a disposable database.
questions.explanation: Describe two-session behavior for a small transaction, then test commit/rollback and one conflict in a disposable database. This makes the result reviewable and aligns with a controlled learning workflow.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “Transaction Design for Application Workflows”, what should be verified?
options: Assume a successful connection means the query and data model are correct.
Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
Ignore version notes and infer behavior from an unrelated database engine.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
questions.explanation: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
